<p>LZ4 只做一件事：遇到前面出現過的資料，就不再存一次，改記「往回幾格、複: LZ4 does only one thing: when it meets data that has already appeared earlier, it does not store it again; instead it records how far back to go and how many bytes to copy. Data that has not appeared before is stored as is; a byte stored this way is called a literal, and the part copied from earlier is called a match.

<li><strong>Literal bytes：</strong>找不到: • Literal bytes: bytes for which no repeat was found and which can only be stored as is.
<li><strong>Descriptor：</strong>告訴解碼器這: • Descriptor: tells the decoder how to rebuild this part. Every part has one, and each answers the same three questions: how many bytes to store as literals, how far back to go, and how many bytes to copy.
<p>解壓縮時，解碼器一段一段照著 descriptor 做：</p>: When decompressing, the decoder follows the descriptors one part at a time:
<li><strong>Descriptor 1：</strong>照存 1: • Descriptor 1: store 14 bytes as literals, giving say:hello-bob-. Then from the current position 14 go back 10, to position 4, and copy 5 bytes, giving hello.
<li><strong>Descriptor 2：</strong>照存 7: • Descriptor 2: store 7 bytes as literals, giving ,again!. This part has nothing to copy, and the rebuild ends here.

<p>LZ4 的設計重點是速度：它不做 Huffman 這類 entropy 編: LZ4 is designed for speed: it does no entropy coding such as Huffman, all lengths are byte-aligned, and decompression needs no bit-by-bit decoding, only repeated copying of data. The price is a lower compression ratio than zstd or Deflate.

<p>Token 不是一個數字，而是兩個各佔 4 bits 的欄位。下圖把 <c: The Token is not one number but two fields of 4 bits each. The figure below splits 0xE1 apart and writes the same bits in three number bases:
<div class=\"fig\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0: <div class="fig"><svg viewBox="0 0 860 176" role="img" aria-label="The 8 bits of Token 0xE1 are 1110 0001. The high 4 bits 1110 equal 0xE, decimal 14, meaning 14 literals; the low 4 bits 0001 equal 0x1, decimal 1, meaning copy 1 plus 4 equals 5 bytes">
<p>前面兩張圖裡有三個約定，它們就是整個格式的核心：</p>: The two figures above contain three conventions, and they are the core of the whole format:
<li><strong>兩個長度放最前面。</strong>解碼器要先知道有: • The two lengths come first. The decoder has to know how many literals there are before it knows where the text ends and where the offset begins. 14 and 5 are both small numbers; each fits in 4 bits, so they are merged into 1 byte, and this byte is called the Token. 14 is 0xE and goes in the high 4 bits.
<li><strong>Match 長度存「長度減 4」。</strong>: • The match length is stored as “length minus 4”. A match costs at least 2 bytes of offset and usually one more Token, so a match shorter than 4 saves almost nothing, and LZ4 defines 4 as the minimum. Since it is never less than 4, a stored 0 means 4, and 5 is stored as 1, which is 0x1, in the low 4 bits. Put the two fields together and the Token is 0xE1.
<li><strong>Offset 固定 2 bytes，低位在前</st: • The offset is always 2 bytes, low byte first (little-endian). It is read back as “first byte + second byte × 256”. 0x0A is 10, so 0x0A 0x00 = 10 + 0 × 256 = 10. A larger one: offset 300 is stored as 0x2C 0x01, where 0x2C is 44 and 0x01 is 1, so 44 + 1 × 256 = 300. 2 bytes can represent at most 65535, so a match can reach back about 64KB at most; repeated data further away cannot be referenced.
<p>所以 descriptor 在真實格式裡不是獨立的一塊，而是拆開放在 li: So in the real format the descriptor is not a separate block; it is split up and placed before and after the literals: how many to store and how many to copy go into the Token, how far back goes into the offset. The group Token, literals, offset is called a sequence, and an LZ4 block is a series of sequences.
<p>Descriptor 只是本文為了說明取的稱呼，LZ4 規格沒有這個詞，它: Descriptor is only a name used in this document for explanation. The LZ4 specification has no such term, and it has nothing to do with the job descriptors the accelerator works with in Section 8.
<li><strong>Literal 長度 14：</strong>這: • Literal length 14: how many new bytes this sequence stores.
<li><strong>Offset 10：</strong>從現在要寫: • Offset 10: how far back from the current write position the source is. The current write position is 14, so the source is at 14 - 10 = position 4.
<li><strong>Match 長度 5：</strong>從來源複: • Match length 5: how many bytes to copy from the source.
<p>Offset 也可以比 literal 長度大，因為來源可以在更早的: The offset can also be larger than the literal length, because the source can lie in an earlier sequence. In the 63-byte example later on, the 4th sequence has literal length 0 but offset 23.

<p>第 9 節提到加速器有自己的 MMU。這一節先從零開始說明它要解決什麼問題: Section 9 mentions that the accelerator has its own MMU. This section starts from zero with the problem it has to solve, and only compares it with the CPU MMU at the end.

The COT (Compressed Object Table) is an array in DRAM with 32 bytes per entry, one fixed entry per compressible page, recording the compressed length, how many chunks are used, and the number of each chunk. When the page currently has no compressed object, the valid flag of its entry is 0.
<p><strong>Handle</strong> 就是 page 在可壓縮範: The handle is the number of the page within the compressible range, and also the index into this array: handle = (VA - 0x7F12_2000_0000) ÷ 4096. <h3>地址翻譯：為什麼叫 MMU</h3>: Address translation: why it is called an MMU
<p>解碼器只想循序讀取壓縮資料，它不該處理「讀完 512 bytes 後要換到: The decoder only wants to read the compressed data sequentially; it should not have to deal with things like “after reading 512 bytes, which address comes next”, so it only asks: where is byte 1100 of object 0x14567? <p>LZ4 MMU 用一個<strong>堆疊</strong>管理空的 ch: The LZ4 MMU manages empty chunks with a stack, that is, a pile of available chunk numbers: during compression, every time the output fills 512B it pops the top one; when an object is freed, its numbers are pushed back. Wherever a chunk is, popping one takes a single step, and no data has to be moved.
<p>275 MiB 的 pool 有 563,200 個 chunk，每個編號: A 275 MiB pool has 563,200 chunks; at 3 bytes per number, the full list is about 1.6 MiB, which does not fit on the chip. So this document stores the stack in two parts:
<li><strong>最上面一段在 LZ4 MMU 的 SRAM：</st: • The top part lives in the SRAM of the LZ4 MMU: at most 512 numbers, 1.5 KB in total. Pops and returns only touch this part, so they never wait for DRAM.
<li><strong>其餘的存在 pool 裡空著的 chunk：</st: • The rest is stored in empty chunks in the pool: such a chunk is called a list chunk. Its first 3 bytes hold the number of the next list chunk, followed by the numbers of 169 empty chunks, 510 bytes in total. List chunks are linked one after another, and the number of the first one is kept in the accelerator register LIST_HEAD.
<li><strong>「沒有下一個」用 <code>0xFFFFFF</c: • “No next” is represented by 0xFFFFFF: 3 bytes hold 24 bits, but the numbers of the 563,200 chunks only use 0x000000 to 0x0897FF, so anything from 0x089800 up is not a legal number, and this document picks 0xFFFFFF. 0 cannot be used, because chunk 0 is a real chunk. The next of the last list chunk is 0xFFFFFF; when there is no list chunk at all, LIST_HEAD is also 0xFFFFFF. If a refill reads a value at or above 0x089800 that is not 0xFFFFFF, the list is corrupt, and the accelerator stops and reports an error.

When the SRAM has fewer than 64 numbers, one list chunk is read back; when it has more than 448, one is written out">
<figcaption>補充時讀回一個 list chunk：裡面的 169: <figcaption>A refill reads back one list chunk: the 169 numbers inside it, plus this chunk itself, 170 in total, return to the SRAM. <p>兩段之間什麼時候搬動：</p>: When numbers move between the two parts:
<li><strong>補充（refill）：</strong>SRAM 少: • Refill: when the SRAM has fewer than 64 numbers, read the chunk that LIST_HEAD points to, put its 169 numbers into the SRAM, and set LIST_HEAD to the next number it recorded. Once read, this chunk is empty too, so its own number goes in as well: one refill adds 170.
<li><strong>溢出（spill）：</strong>SRAM 超過: • Spill: when the SRAM has more than 448 numbers, take one number from the SRAM as the new list chunk, write the old LIST_HEAD and 169 numbers into it, then point LIST_HEAD at it. The SRAM thus loses 170.
<p>兩個門檻離得很遠：補充後最多 233 個，溢出後至少 279 個，所以不會: The two thresholds are far apart: after a refill there are at most 233 numbers, and after a spill at least 279, so the stack never spills right after a refill and shuttles back and forth. One compression uses at most 7 chunks, and a refill is triggered only when the count drops below 64, which leaves plenty of margin to wait for DRAM to respond. Each move is just one 512B DRAM access, and it happens on average once every 170 pops or returns. At boot, the RO objects already occupy the chunks at the start of the pool; the kernel issues one initialization command, and the accelerator writes the remaining chunks as a linked list of list chunks. Only when both the SRAM and the list chunks run out does it report POOL_FULL. The example at the end of Section 12 has only 24 chunks, so the whole stack fits in the SRAM; no list chunk appears there, and LIST_HEAD stays 0xFFFFFF.
<h3>CTLB：不要一直查 COT</h3>: CTLB: do not keep looking up the COT
<p>COT 在 DRAM 裡，每查一次都要等 DRAM。解碼一個物件時，每換一: The COT is in DRAM, and every lookup waits for DRAM. While decoding an object, the next chunk number is needed every time the chunk changes; if each one were a lookup, 5 chunks would cost 5 extra DRAM reads. But the 32 bytes read the first time already contain all the numbers, so it is enough to keep them in a small cache inside the accelerator. That is the CTLB.
<p>它和 CPU 的 TLB 目的相同，但小得多。本文的 SoC 只有一個 e: It serves the same purpose as the TLB of the CPU, but is much smaller. The SoC in this document has only one engine and decompresses one object at a time, so the CTLB holds only 1 entry: the 32-byte COT entry of the object currently being decompressed. When the next object starts, the old entry is overwritten.

An RW object is freed as soon as it is decompressed; an RO object stays forever, but it is read again only after the page is evicted from the frame cache and then used again, which is a long time later, and by then the CTLB has long since moved on to other objects. So when an RW object is freed, the kernel has to issue an INVALIDATE command to clear it: when the same page is compressed again later, a new chunk list is written under the same handle, and if the CTLB still held the old one, it would read the wrong chunks.
